summary: render assistant messages as markdown — DeepSeek (and likely Claude) emit MD that currently shows as literal **/##/etc
description:
DeepSeek output uses standard markdown — '## Heading', '**bold**', bullet lists, code fences, blockquotes — and it's being rendered as plain text in the chat UI because <ChatView> just does {msg.text}.

Plan:
- Add react-markdown + remark-gfm (for tables/strikethrough/task lists/autolinks).
- New <MarkdownMessage> wrapper (kept inline in chat-view for now) with style-token component overrides for h1-h4, p, strong/em, ul/ol/li, code (inline + block), pre, blockquote, a.
- Match the existing aesthetic: display font for prose, mono for code, accent color for links, subtle borders for blockquotes/code blocks.
- Streaming-friendly: react-markdown re-parses on every update; partial markdown during streaming will 'settle' as content arrives.
- Only assistant messages (role='assistant') get markdown. User messages stay plain text — they typed those literally.

Done when:
- npm install react-markdown remark-gfm.
- ChatView renders msg.text via the markdown component for assistant messages.
- Headings, bold, italic, bulleted/numbered lists, inline + block code, blockquotes, links all render correctly with the existing token system.
- Stream still 'feels' live (no jank from re-parsing on each chunk).
- Test asserts the markdown component is wired in for assistant role only.
